effectiveContext.name: Significant Astro UI implementation profile v2
effectiveContext.selectionRule: Full files initially required or directly routed for an Astro UI task with page-specific styling, accessibility, and explicit bundle-isolation requirements. Matching design-system inventory entries and implementation sources are queried later and are not represented as whole loaded files.

overallSummary: The significant Astro UI profile now routes directly to the documentation and skills needed for the declared work, keeps workflow and review references conditional, and gives exact package commands one authoritative source. The remaining precision cost is within the broad performance playbook: bundle-isolation guidance is required for this profile, but several media and third-party sections are not.
strengths: AGENTS.md explicitly distinguishes coding-agent authority from human-facing documentation and names source-of-truth files.
Task routing exposes architecture, design-system, accessibility, performance, Storybook, specification, and Context Health entry points without loading unrelated routes by default.
Only the safe-change skill is universal for implementation; Astro, performance, UI, search, SEO, Context Health, writing, and voice-analysis skills are conditional.
Package scripts remain authoritative, while the agent documentation validator checks routed links, heading anchors, and documented script names.

priorities.finding: The performance skill is correctly routed for this profile's bundle-isolation requirement, but loading the whole file also includes media, font, analytics, and third-party guidance that the declared task may not use.
priorities.recommendation: Keep the current route until repeated audits justify smaller performance playbooks; when loading the full skill, assess its unrelated sections as a Context Precision cost.

assessed.evidenceMaturityReason: Relevance and within-file precision are documented judgments; citation targets are validated, but representative task loading has not been observed.
assessed.interpretation: The loaded files are task-relevant and directly routed; the broad performance playbook contains the profile's required isolation guidance alongside unrelated media and third-party checks.
limitations: The score applies only to the declared significant Astro UI profile and its full-file loading assumptions.
Semantic relevance judgments are agent-assessed, not inferred from retrieval traces.

checks.label: Repeated command summaries avoid redundant context
checks.interpretation: The authority file keeps a small validation summary, the README keeps a human quick start, and testing documentation owns the complete check guidance.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md names package.json as exact authority and points to testing guidance; README lists five primary commands; docs/testing.md contains the full validation reference.

observed.interpretation: No representative task runs have been evaluated for this metric.
limitations: No observed-performance claim can be made until a versioned suite records representative tasks, configurations, and outcomes.

assessed.evidenceMaturityReason: Deterministic checks confirm the declared routes and evidence targets; representative tasks have not yet tested whether required context is actually loaded.
assessed.interpretation: The authority file directly exposes the major task routes, matching specifications, Storybook guidance, design-system sources, and conditional skills required by this profile.

details.estimationMethod: Estimated tokens = ceil(UTF-16 code units / 4). This is an approximation, not a tokenizer result.

methodology.scoreCalculation: For each statically assessed scored metric, contribution = check weight × result score. Weights total 1; the assessed score is the sum. Status records whether the finite current checks are complete or contain gaps, not universal health.
methodology.assessmentBoundary: Static assessment inspects declared repository context and structure. Observed evaluation requires representative task runs and remains not measured in this report. The two modes must not be combined into an aggregate score.

tokenEstimation.note: The generator reports JavaScript string length after UTF-8 decoding. This is not a byte count, Unicode-code-point count, actual retrieved context, or tokenizer result.

evidenceMaturityLevels.definition: A documented claim supported by identified evidence and explicit limitations.
Deterministic checks confirm the relevant files, links, headings, scripts, precedence, or report structure.
At least one representative task run supplies direct performance evidence.
Multiple representative runs show the result across declared agents or configurations.
Repeated results remain acceptable under versioned perturbation or conflict challenges.

limitations: No complete open standard currently combines repository context routing, static readiness, observed task performance, evidence maturity, and profile coverage. Context Health Core 0.1 is an experimental project methodology.
Semantic findings are an agent assessment of repository guidance, not a measurement of model behavior or output quality.
All observed results are not measured. No task runs, agents, configurations, evaluation suites, confidence estimates, or variation estimates are claimed.
This report preserves significant Astro UI profile v2 as its static baseline; the static checks, weights, evidence, audited revision, and scores are unchanged.

The declared effective-context set contains full files initially required or directly routed for this profile. Matching inventory entries and implementation sources consulted later are task-dependent and excluded from the deterministic full-file measurement.

Active Context Size uses JavaScript string length (UTF-16 code units) after UTF-8 decoding. The four-code-units-per-token estimate is deliberately simple and can differ materially from a real tokenizer.
The repository revision identifies the audited baseline commit. It does not claim to identify the later commit that contains this report.
